items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: You know Joe saw to it that the saxophone section phrased and breathed together, and Pat, you know, everybody knew he was the leader. So we had good guys that were used to working with one another.

ctx.x: But things like music contracting, those take another skill. You have to be pretty darn organized and, did you find, yeah I can do that stuff.

Yes. And I’m not pretty darn organized. I just, I don’t know, I just was kind of, well first of all I just fell into it like everything else. You know things just happened. An opportunity is there and you do it, and it wasn’t a conscious thinking now I’ve got to do this or that. Just like playing. It kind of took me along for the ride. But I’m fortunate because I’m involved with the Central NY Jazz Orchestra and we have a working big band, and I have an opportunity to do arranging when I want to, in an organized,…
whenever there were strings involved it was usually the Syracuse Symphony people. Yeah. Did I answer your question?
